# Platform Overview, Licensing & Community

Reference file for [citations.md](../citations.md).

## What Is Windmill?

Windmill is an open-source workflow engine and developer platform that turns
scripts into webhooks, workflows, and UIs [1]. Built by Windmill Labs (Paris,
France), it was founded by Ruben Fiszel in 2022 as part of Y Combinator's
W22 batch [18].

The platform is code-first: users write scripts in supported languages, and
Windmill handles execution, scheduling, error handling, and UI generation.
It supports Python, TypeScript (Deno and Bun runtimes), Go, PHP, Bash, C#,
SQL, Rust, Ruby, R, GraphQL, PowerShell, and arbitrary Docker images [3].

## Architecture

| Layer | Technology | Purpose |
|-------|-----------|---------|
| Backend | Rust | API server, job orchestration |
| Frontend | Svelte | Web UI and editor |
| Database | PostgreSQL | State, job queue, secrets |
| Workers | Language-specific runtimes | Job execution |
| Expression engine | QuickJS (default) or Deno/V8 (EE) | Flow data transforms |

Source: [3][4][12]

The architecture is stateless API servers + PostgreSQL + workers. Workers pull
jobs from a PostgreSQL-backed queue, execute them, and store results back.
Each step in a flow is a separate job picked up by a worker [12][13].

Workflow definitions use the OpenFlow JSON format — a JSON-serializable
specification consisting of an input spec and sequential steps [12].

## Licensing

| Aspect | Details | Source |
|--------|---------|--------|
| Core license | AGPL-3.0 | [2][40] |
| OSI compliant | Yes (approved March 3, 2008) | [40] |
| Enterprise Edition | Commercial license | [16] |
| GitHub license field | "NOASSERTION" (mixed licensing) | [2] |

The Community Edition is licensed under AGPL-3.0, which is OSI-approved [40].
However, the GitHub repository reports "NOASSERTION" because the codebase
contains mixed licensing — AGPL-3.0 and Apache 2.0 sources alongside
proprietary EE-only code [2].

### AGPL-3.0 Implications for Personal Use

AGPL-3.0 requires source disclosure when modified software is made available
over a network. For personal use on a home workstation with no external
access, AGPL has no practical restrictions — it behaves like GPL [40].

### Community vs Enterprise Edition

| Core workflow engine | Yes | Yes |

| Max users | 50 | Unlimited |
| Max workspaces | 3 | Unlimited |
| SSO users | 10 max | Unlimited |
| Audit logs | Redacted | Full (60+ days) |

| SAML/SCIM | No | Yes |
| Worker group management UI | No | Yes |
| Concurrency limits | No | Yes |
| Content search | No | Yes |
| Full-text search on jobs/logs | No | Yes |
| Multiplayer IDE | No | Yes |
| S3 log streaming | No | Yes |
| White labeling | No | Yes |

Source: [16][17]

### Pricing (Self-Hosted)

| Plan | Price | Eligibility |
|------|-------|-------------|
| Community | $0/mo | Anyone |
| Pro | From $120/mo | <10 employees, <$250K revenue |
| Enterprise | From $120/mo | Custom pricing |

Compute units: 1 CU = 2 worker-GB-month. Standard 2GB worker = 1 CU at
$50/worker/mo. Native workers: $50/mo for 8 workers [17].

Developer seats: $20/mo. Operator seats: $10/mo [17].

### Licensing Controversy

GitHub Issue #5014 raised concerns about marketing as "open-source" while
gating features behind EE. The founder responded that Windmill is
"commercial open-source" with $1M+ ARR and 150+ enterprise customers,
at break-even. The original poster retracted criticism after further
research [19].

## Gaps and Limitations

- Exact encryption algorithm not documented (symmetric key described but
  not whether AES, ChaCha20, etc.) [7]
- Percentage split of AGPL vs Apache 2.0 vs proprietary code not quantified
- Community contributor activity metrics (PRs/month, response times) not
  found in accessible sources
- No third-party security audit results published (SOC 2 Type II compliance
  mentioned but audit report not public) [7]
